predecessors.name: Oirat Confederation (17th century)
predecessors.text: the Oirat homeland on the upper Irtysh that the Torghut and some Dorbets left in 1618

predecessors.name: Nogai Horde
predecessors.text: the lower Volga north of the Caspian, 'land that was once part of the Astrakhan Khanate', from which the Oirats expelled the Nogai majority

successors.name: Russian Empire
successors.text: the Kalmyk steppe between the Volga and the Don, north of the Caspian

ledger.x: 1630: the Oirats arrive on the lower Volga and found the Kalmyk Khanate.

c. 1632: the Kalmyks break the first Nogai group. 'The first group was broken up circa 1632 by the Kalmyks'; 'In the early 17th century, the Horde broke down further under the onslaught of the Kalmyks.' The zone is the one the nogai-horde dossier uses for the same contest.
1634: the Volga-Yaik steppe passes to the Kalmyks.
1636: the Kalmyk shape triples, to the North Caucasus steppe.
1738: the Kalmyk shape grows by about 12,000 km2.
October 1771: Catherine II abolishes the Kalmyk Khanate.

wars.name: Kalmyk conquest of the lower Volga
wars.outcome: The Oirats settle on the lower Volga (1630), break the first Nogai group (c.

wars.name: Kalmyk campaigns in the North Caucasus and Kuban
wars.outcome: Raids and Russian-allied campaigns without a dated frontier: Kabardia 1644, Astarabad 1650, Crimea and Nogais 1658, the Kuban attack of 1711 (20,474 Kalmyks and 4,100 Russians; 11,460 Nogais killed) and campaigns in the Kuban and Crimea in 1735.

wars.name: Kalmyk exodus of 1771
wars.outcome: About 169,000 Kalmyks left the Volga for Dzungaria in January 1771 and about 70,000 arrived; the khanate was abolished in October.

certainty.note: A nomad khanate on the open steppe between the Russian settlements and the Caspian; no page gives a boundary line, and Russia's frontier with it is not described.
